posts.title: Radical thoughtfulness: the value of open source
posts.description: What does it mean to share something for other people to use in a world where it is easier than ever, for better or for worse, to whip up something just for yourself? When there are more machines trying to use your tool than people, how does that change where you put your time and energy? Some reflections from the Open Source Arts Contributors Conference about where we go from here.

posts.title: Remember: your work is good!
posts.description: I wrote back in late 2024 about the open source philosophy of p5.js: it aims to not just be a tool you use, but a tool you feel empowered to help shape and maintain, and a community to help you do so. Now, it's fall 2026, and it bears repeating that we do not expect perfect contributions, and that we are here to help you learn and grow.

posts.title: Video editing with p5.js
posts.description: My last animation was created entirely with p5.js visuals, but edited together in an environment with both an IDE and a timeline. Let's walk through how that works!
